To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a method to generate stable hybridomas that express tumor-associated antigen and co-stimulatory molecule, and that these cells are suitable for use as tumor vaccines or for in vitro expansion of tumor-specific CTL.

the development of stable hybridomas for vaccination or for CTL generation is limited by the lack of expression of MHC Class I and II antigens as well as co-stimulatory molecule expression by many tumor cell lines.
we have developed a method for producing stable hybridoma cells that express MHC and co-stimulatory molecule antigens, as well as tumor antigens.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel vaccine for pediatric tumors.
the development of stable tumor cell lines for the production of tumor-specific CTL or as tumor vaccine candidates.
the development of tumor vaccines and tumor-specific cytotoxic lymphocytes for the treatment of pediatric solid tumors, such as neuroblastoma, neuroepithelial tumors, and sarcomas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the fusion of a B lymphoblast and a tumor cell line can produce a hybridoma that is capable of presenting tumor antigen in the context of the host's MHC molecules and that is capable of expressing co-stimulatory factors.

the fusion of B lymphoblasstoid cells expressing puromycin resistance with tumor cells transduced with neomycin resistance allows the generation of stable hybridomas expressing MHC and co-stimulatory molecule.
the use of retroviral vector encoding neomycin and puromycin resistance genes in the generation of stable hybridomas for tumor vaccine or CTL expansion is feasible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel approach to the generation of hybridomas for the development of cancer vaccines or the generation of tumor-specific CTL.
we have successfully produced stable hybridomas for the production of a tumor vaccine.
we have produced a stable hybridoma cell line which is capable of presenting tumor antigens in an immunogenic fashion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of stable tumor hybridomas for use in vaccine or CTL generation is feasible.
fusion of a lymphoblastoid B cell line with a tumor cell line can be used to produce a stable hybridoma that expresses tumor-associated antigens as well as key costimulatory molecules.
the use of retroviral vectors encoding antibiotic resistance genes can facilitate the generation of hybridomas that can be used to generate CTL or as tumor vaccines.
